I will do it close to what I did last year, then push a little where I think the money can come back. I have 16.1 mu, and with wheat-maize I do not count the land like one blank sheet. The wheat land becomes maize land after harvest, so I arrange the year that way. Around here, if I cut fertilizer too hard and the stand turns weak, that loss is bigger than spending a few hundred yuan more, so I would rather feed the crop enough. I finished primary school, so I do pay attention to things like soil strength, irrigation timing, and whether the variety is steady, but I still trust what I saw in nearby fields most. If a neighbor planted a new seed and it stood well, resisted lodging, and gave more jin per mu, I will follow. With well irrigation, I can keep wheat and garlic safer, so I will put the better land and more water toward them. Cotton needs more labor and more sprays, so I will not expand it too much. Garlic brings cash but costs more in seed and management, so I will keep it at a size I can handle. Wheat and maize are still my backbone, so I will keep most of the land there and use hybrid maize and improved wheat seed, give wheat 4 waterings if the spring is dry, maize 2 waterings, garlic 5 small waterings, and cotton 3 waterings. I will use rotary tillage for wheat and garlic because it saves time, no-tillage maize after wheat to catch the season fast, and plough the cotton ground once so the root can go down better.
